AllocationSummary.description: Strategy provenance (spec §8): heuristic or CP-SAT, with each CP-SAT stage's status.
AllocationSummary.title: AllocationSummary

ClockWindow.description:
Service-start window in local clock time. `fold` picks the occurrence of an ambiguous
(fall-back) time and applies to both ends. earliest > latest is a preflight finding.
ClockWindow.title: ClockWindow

ClusterWarmStart.description:
One cluster's warm-start outcome. `initial_cost` is PyVRP's objective of the mapped plan on
this run's problem; `final_cost` is the objective PyVRP returned starting from it (never higher
with a feasible start: tests/test_warm_start.py).
ClusterWarmStart.title: ClusterWarmStart

CoordinateOrigin.description:
A location's first coordinate, kept with its provenance when a manual correction or an
explicit re-geocode replaces it (spec §6: keep original and corrected provenance).
CoordinateOrigin.title: CoordinateOrigin

ExplorerSettings.description:
A clustering-only job: no allocation changes, no PyVRP. `base` supplies the population
(eligible, allocated locations) and the spatial policy; ks × seeds are the k-means tasks and
each H3 resolution is one deterministic task. All of them count toward the task cap.
ExplorerSettings.title: ExplorerSettings

GeocodeMatch.description:
How an address became a coordinate (spec §6). Records the match, never a confidence score.

Census matches are interpolated along address ranges, not rooftop points. ZCTA matches are
the Gazetteer internal point of the ZIP Code Tabulation Area with the same code as the ZIP.
GeocodeMatch.title: GeocodeMatch

LabClient.description:
A visit created directly (spec §5: no order needed). Delivery is per dimension id; a
dimension left out delivers 0.
LabClient.title: LabClient

LabDimension.description: A named load dimension (units, weight, volume or any user-defined resource).
LabDimension.title: LabDimension

LabGroup.description:
Mutually exclusive alternatives (PyVRP ClientGroup): at most one member is visited. A
``required`` group must be served by exactly one member (a customer reachable at one of
several service points); an optional group may be left unserved. Members are optional clients
(``required: false``) without a prize of their own, so the group, not a prize, decides.
LabGroup.title: LabGroup

LabGroupOutcome.description: Which member (if any) serves a group.
LabGroupOutcome.title: LabGroupOutcome

LabObjective.description:
Nominal objective recomputed from the instance (PyVRP 0.14 semantics): per used vehicle
its fixed cost, plus unit_distance_cost × route distance and unit_duration_cost × route
duration. ``total`` is this nominal cost only. Infeasibility penalties are never part of it.
With optional clients PyVRP minimizes ``total`` plus the prizes of the clients it skips:
``uncollected_prizes`` is reported as its own term and ``objective_with_prizes`` is the sum
PyVRP optimized. Prizes are in the instance's cost unit but are never costs.
LabObjective.title: LabObjective

LabPair.description:
A pickup-delivery pair (PyVRP Shipment): ``amount`` (per dimension) is loaded at the pickup
stop and unloaded at the delivery stop, on the same vehicle, pickup first. While it is on
board it counts against the vehicle's capacity.
LabPair.title: LabPair

LabPairOutcome.description: Where each pair was served: both stops on one route, pickup before delivery.
LabPairOutcome.title: LabPairOutcome

LabSkipped.description: An optional client that no route visits, and the prize forgone.
LabSkipped.title: LabSkipped

LabSolver.description:
Seed and stopping criteria. With ``max_iterations`` the run stops after that many
iterations (reproducible across machines) unless the runtime cap is hit first; without it,
the runtime alone stops the search (machine dependent).
LabSolver.title: LabSolver

LabStop.description:
A place a pickup-delivery pair visits: a pickup point or a delivery point. Stop ids share the
namespace of depots and clients.
LabStop.title: LabStop

LabTravel.description: Geographic only: haversine × circuity meters, and seconds at a constant speed.
LabTravel.title: LabTravel

LabTrip.description:
One trip of a route: from the route's start depot or a reload depot to the next reload
depot or the route's end depot. Loads are per trip (full again after every reload).
LabTrip.title: LabTrip

LabVehicleType.description:
A vehicle type with a finite count. Every vehicle starts at ``start_depot`` and ends at
``end_depot`` (depot ids; both default to the first depot, so a single-depot instance needs
neither). Routes are closed in the sense that every route returns to a depot; there is no open
route workaround. Capacity names every dimension.
LabVehicleType.title: LabVehicleType

PreflightFinding.description: One preflight check that found something. `action` is what the run did about it.
PreflightFinding.title: PreflightFinding

PreflightPolicy.description:
M2 scope item 8: which preflight checks stop a run. Policy, not physics (§7).

Round two (spec v1.9): `far_from_depot` covers only stops no chain of allowed drives
reaches; a far stop reachable through another stop is the warning `far_via_stop`. A stop
larger than one trailer splits across shipments by default.
PreflightPolicy.title: PreflightPolicy

TimeModel.description:
Single-day time model (spec §5): clock strings are local to `timezone` on `planning_date`
and normalize to elapsed integer seconds from local midnight. `horizon_end` may pass 24:00
(late shifts), at most 48:00. `depot_open` is when trucks leave the depot.
TimeModel.title: TimeModel

TimeSummary.description: The time model a time-window run used; `*_s` values are seconds from local midnight.
TimeSummary.title: TimeSummary

TravelSummary.description: Which travel data the run used (spec §7): estimated, or a stored directed snapshot.
TravelSummary.title: TravelSummary

WarmStartCluster.description: A source cluster: validated ones carry their routes in service order; others carry none.
WarmStartCluster.title: WarmStartCluster

WarmStartPlan.description:
The warm-start source interface (spec §10, M6): a plan as routes of visits with their
location and load, per source cluster, and the travel it was validated on. Its content hash is
the plan identity recorded in the `warm_start` stage artifact and the replay bundle.
WarmStartPlan.title: WarmStartPlan

WarmStartSource.description:
Where a warm start's plan comes from (spec §10, M6). Today only a succeeded pipeline run the
submitter can read; the web resolves it with owner checks and the worker receives its validated
plan over the loopback transport as a `WarmStartPlan`. Another source (a saved manual baseline)
would be a new `kind` producing the same plan document.
WarmStartSource.title: WarmStartSource

WarmStartTravel.description:
The travel identity the source plan was validated on: estimated haversine × circuity, or
a stored directed snapshot.
WarmStartTravel.title: WarmStartTravel
